```{=typst}
#set page(numbering: "I")
#counter(page).update(3)
```

The fixture for the order of Typst locators and the pages a range spans
(M100). A locator's class comes from its page's numbering: lower roman `i`,
upper roman `I`, arabic `1`, lower letters `a`, upper letters `A`, then any
other symbol or a numbering function. A page with no numbering is arabic.
Its value is the page counter's value, or the physical page on a page with no
numbering. An entry's locators print in class order, then by value, then by
physical page.

Every page starts at a raw Typst `set page` rule, which starts a new page
itself, and each rule but the one for page 13, which has no numbering, is
followed by a page counter update. So the physical
page, the pattern and the counter value of each page are facts of this source.
The manifest, tests/typst-order.tsv, states them from here and nowhere else.
Each term is one case, and no two cases share an entry.

## Physical page 1

The pattern is `I` and the counter is 3, so the page prints `III`.

Upper roman, marked before lower roman: [ash]{.index}.

```{=typst}
#set page(numbering: "1")
#counter(page).update(3)
```

## Physical page 2

The pattern is `1` and the counter is 3.

Arabic, marked before upper roman: [beech]{.index}.

A mark before a reset, with a higher value than a mark after it:
[hazel]{.index}.

A value that the range of `kale` spans, on a page outside that range:
[kale]{.index}.

```{=typst}
#set page(numbering: "i")
#counter(page).update(2)
```

## Physical page 3

The pattern is `i` and the counter is 2, so the page prints `ii`.

The second mark of `ash`: [ash]{.index}.

```{=typst}
#set page(numbering: "I")
#counter(page).update(2)
```

The pattern is `1` and the counter is 2.

A page of one class and value that prints another text than the next page:

A range whose two ends have one value and print different texts:

A range whose two ends print one text: [nutmeg]{.index range="open"}.

```{=typst}

#counter(page).update(2)
```
